findings.F1: The tested idea's gain sits only in the widest days, not across a gradient. On the 3-day grid, up-run days in the widest range quintile were followed by +1.30 % excess (t 2.16, 1133 cases, 374 days), while quintiles 0 to 3 gave -0.03 %, -0.00 %, -0.03 % and -0.50 % (all |t| < 1.2).
findings.F2: The widest up-run days followed through only in rising-market years. Their 3-day excess was +2.94 % in 2020, +4.40 % in 2021, +1.16 % in 2023 and +2.23 % in 2024, but -2.85 % in 2018, -1.99 % in 2022 and -0.55 % in 2025. No single year reached |t| 2.2.
findings.F3: The book's gain mostly follows the market. Its mean daily return is 0.080 % against the coins' 0.139 %. Its sign by year matches the coins' sign in 7 of 8 years (2018, where the book lost 0.016 % a day against the coins' 0.349 %, softened rather than reversed). Its best 5 % of days sum to +5.53 against a total of +2.31.

findings.F5: Down-run days that close near their high were followed by a further fall, -1.19 % over 3 days (t -1.98, 728 cases, 255 days), negative in 6 of 8 years. But it is not graded: the slope of excess return on close location within down-runs has t -0.64 (4993 cases), and at 6 days the effect fades to -0.82 % (t -0.58).
findings.F6: Other angles gave isolated cells near |t| 2 and no graded pattern, against roughly 80 cells examined:

no_ideas: Across about 80 cells (range, close location, body, run, 5- and 20-day returns, volatility, weekday, year, and 3- and 6-day horizons), no pattern beyond the tested idea is both graded and clearly stronger than chance; the best cells reach only |t| about 2, which so many looks would produce by chance.
